advanced_desc_active_checking: The maximum number of torrents that are checked at the same time.
advanced_desc_active_dht_limit: The maximum number of torrents announced to the DHT.
advanced_desc_active_lsd_limit: The maximum number of torrents announced to the local network with Local Service Discovery.
advanced_desc_active_tracker_limit: The maximum number of torrents announced to their trackers.
advanced_desc_allowed_fast_set_size: The number of allowed-fast pieces sent to peers that support the Fast extension.
advanced_desc_allow_multiple_connections: Allow more than one connection from the same IP address. Rejecting them prevents abuse by peers; detecting duplicate peers is more complicated when this is enabled and more likely to fail in edge cases. Enabling it is not recommended.
advanced_desc_announce_to_all_tiers: For torrents with several trackers: when enabled, one tracker from every tier is announced to (uTorrent behavior). Disable to follow the multi-tracker specification.
advanced_desc_announce_to_all_trackers: For torrents with several trackers: when enabled, all trackers in a tier are announced to in parallel, and if all trackers in tier 0 fail, the trackers in tier 1 are announced to as well. When disabled, the multi-tracker specification is followed.
advanced_desc_anonymous_mode: Hide the client identity where possible: the user agent is emptied (except for private torrents), trackers are only used through a proxy, the listen sockets are closed and incoming connections are only accepted through a SOCKS5 or I2P proxy. NAT-PMP, UPnP, DHT and local peer discovery are turned off.
advanced_desc_auto_manage_interval: The number of seconds between updates and rotations of the torrent queue.
advanced_desc_auto_manage_prefer_seeds: When handing out active slots, prefer seeding torrents. When disabled, downloading torrents are preferred.
advanced_desc_auto_scrape_interval: The number of seconds between scrapes of queued (automatically managed and paused) torrents. The resulting seed/leecher ratio decides which torrents are seeded and which are paused.
advanced_desc_auto_scrape_min_interval: The minimum number of seconds between any two automatic scrapes, regardless of torrent. Limits how often scrapes are sent when many automatically managed torrents are paused.
advanced_desc_checking_mem_usage: The number of 16 KiB blocks kept outstanding while checking torrents. Higher values make re-checks faster but use more memory.
advanced_desc_choking_algorithm: How the number of unchoked peers is determined. Downloading torrents always unchoke the peers they download fastest from (tit-for-tat). Options: 0 = fixed slots, 2 = rate based.
advanced_desc_connection_speed: The number of outgoing connection attempts per second. A negative value means 200 per second, 0 disables outgoing connections.
advanced_desc_disk_write_mode: Whether disk writes go through memory-mapped files or regular write calls. Only affects the memory-mapped disk backend; with libtorrent 2.1 PicoTorrent uses the pread/pwrite backend on Windows, so this has no effect. Options: 0 = always pwrite, 1 = always mmap write, 2 = automatic.
advanced_desc_dont_count_slow_torrents: Torrents without payload transfer do not count towards the active download and seed limits, so idle torrents do not block active slots and all available bandwidth is more likely to be used.
advanced_desc_file_pool_size: The maximum number of files kept open by the session. Files are kept open because some antivirus software scans every file on close; most systems also limit how many files a process may have open.
advanced_desc_hashing_threads: The number of threads used to verify piece hashes when checking torrents (they also read the data from disk). More threads verify faster on SSDs and help v2 torrents; on hard drives 1 is usually best. PicoTorrent defaults to 2.
advanced_desc_inactive_down_rate: The download rate (bytes per second) below which a torrent counts as inactive for queuing. A torrent below both the inactive download and upload rates can make room for another queued torrent. Only used when dont_count_slow_torrents is enabled.
advanced_desc_inactive_up_rate: The upload rate (bytes per second) below which a torrent counts as inactive for queuing. A torrent below both the inactive download and upload rates can make room for another queued torrent. Only used when dont_count_slow_torrents is enabled.
advanced_desc_inactivity_timeout: Disconnect a peer after this many seconds if neither side is interested in the other.
advanced_desc_incoming_starts_queued_tor: Start a torrent that was paused by the queue when a peer connects for it. Queuing mostly saves on announces and unchoke slots, so a peer that found us anyway can still be served.
advanced_desc_initial_picker_threshold: The number of pieces picked at random before switching to rarest-first piece picking.
advanced_desc_listen_queue_size: The backlog passed to listen(): how many incoming connections may wait to be accepted. 5 is enough for normal use. Takes effect when the listen interfaces change.
advanced_desc_max_allowed_in_request_que: The number of block requests a peer may queue up with us. Further requests are dropped. Higher values allow faster uploads to a single peer.
advanced_desc_max_failcount: How many times connecting to a peer may fail before giving up on it. A successful connection resets the counter; hearing about the peer again from any source except the DHT allows another try.
advanced_desc_max_out_request_queue: The maximum number of outstanding block requests sent to a peer, regardless of download speed.
advanced_desc_max_peer_recv_buffer_size: The maximum size, in bytes, of a single peer connection's receive buffer.
advanced_desc_max_queued_disk_bytes: The maximum number of bytes waiting to be written to disk. When reached, peer connections stop reading from their sockets until the disk catches up. Setting this too low severely limits the download rate.
advanced_desc_max_rejects: The number of piece requests in a row rejected while a peer is choked before the peer is considered abusive and disconnected.
advanced_desc_min_reconnect_time: The number of seconds to wait before reconnecting to a peer, multiplied by its fail count.
advanced_desc_mixed_mode_algorithm: How TCP connections are treated when uTP connections are present. uTP yields to TCP, so without a limit uTP peers get starved. Options: 0 = prefer TCP, 1 = limit TCP to its proportional share of the peers.
advanced_desc_mmap_file_size_cutoff: Files smaller than this number of 16 KiB blocks are not memory-mapped. Only affects the memory-mapped disk backend, which PicoTorrent does not use on Windows with libtorrent 2.1.
advanced_desc_no_atime_storage: Open files with O_NOATIME. Linux only, has no effect on Windows.
advanced_desc_peer_timeout: Seconds without any activity before a peer connection is closed. The protocol specifies 120 seconds; a keep-alive is sent after half of it.
advanced_desc_peer_turnover: The percentage of peers disconnected every peer_turnover_interval when the peer limit is reached, to make room for possibly better peers.
advanced_desc_peer_turnover_cutoff: Peer turnover only starts when connected to more than this percentage of the peer limit.
advanced_desc_peer_turnover_interval: The number of seconds between peer turnover rounds.
advanced_desc_predictive_piece_announce: When greater than 0, announce pieces to peers this many milliseconds before they are expected to finish downloading (and before hash checking), saving round trips per piece.
advanced_desc_rate_choker_initial_thresh: The starting upload rate threshold of the rate based choker. A higher value gives fewer unchoke slots, a lower value more.
advanced_desc_request_timeout: Seconds within which a 16 KiB block is expected to arrive. Otherwise it is requested from another peer.
advanced_desc_seed_choking_algorithm: How peers are picked for unchoking on seeding torrents, where tit-for-tat does not apply. Options: 0 = round robin, 1 = fastest upload, 2 = anti-leech.
advanced_desc_seed_time_ratio_limit: A seeding torrent is considered done when seconds seeding divided by seconds downloading reaches this value (in percent). Done torrents can still seed, they just lose their priority in the queue.
advanced_desc_send_buffer_low_watermark: The minimum send buffer target in bytes, including data pending read from disk. Works as the initial window that decides how fast the upload rate can ramp up. Too small hurts upload speed, too large wastes memory.
advanced_desc_send_buffer_watermark: The upper limit of the send buffer in bytes. When fewer bytes than this are buffered, another 16 KiB block is read from disk.
advanced_desc_send_buffer_watermark_fact: The current upload rate to a peer multiplied by this percentage gives its send buffer size, capped by send_buffer_watermark. Above 100 helps high-speed uploads, too high wastes memory.
advanced_desc_send_not_sent_low_watermar: The not-sent low watermark for socket send buffers (TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT). Linux only.
advanced_desc_share_ratio_limit: A seeding torrent is considered done when uploaded divided by downloaded reaches this value (in percent). Done torrents can still seed, they just lose their priority in the queue.
advanced_desc_stop_tracker_timeout: Seconds to wait for a tracker to answer the stopped event before giving up. Kept short so the client exits quickly; 0 skips stopped announces.
advanced_desc_strict_end_game_mode: Only request a block a second time when every remaining piece has at least one request. Can slow down some pieces but avoids downloading redundant data. When disabled, every peer connection is kept busy even with duplicate requests.
advanced_desc_suggest_mode: Whether to send suggest messages that bias peers towards requesting particular pieces. Options: 0 = no suggestions, 1 = suggest pieces from the read cache.
advanced_desc_torrent_connect_boost: The number of peers connected to immediately after the first tracker response, to speed up new torrents instead of waiting for the connection scheduler. At most 255.
advanced_desc_unchoke_slots_limit: The maximum number of unchoked peers in the session; may be ignored depending on the choking algorithm. -1 means unlimited.
advanced_desc_use_parole_mode: Peers that took part in a piece that failed the hash check may only download whole pieces from then on. If such a whole piece fails again the peer is banned; a piece that passes clears the parole.
advanced_desc_whole_pieces_threshold: If a whole piece can be downloaded from a peer within this many seconds, request whole pieces from it. Makes disk access more local and bad peers easier to identify.
advanced_desc_save_resume_data_interval: The interval in seconds between saving resume data for torrents (and the DHT node cache), so state survives an unexpected exit.
advanced_desc_torrent_overview_columns: The number of columns in the torrent overview panel.
advanced_desc_torrent_overview_show_piec: Show the piece progress bar in the torrent overview panel.
